name: Park Hyatt Auckland
positioning: Waterfront hotel in Auckland's Wynyard Quarter, looking across the Lighter Basin to the Waitemata Harbour, with interiors by Conran and Partners
best_for: Travelers who want a harbourside base in Wynyard Quarter
Guests who like to eat and drink on site, with several waterfront venues to choose from

facts.text: The hotel sits on the water's edge, with views across Wynyard Quarter's Lighter Basin and out to the Waitemata Harbour.
Wynyard Quarter is a docklands precinct converted into the America's Cup home base.
Dining includes Onemata, The Living Room, The Pantry, Captain's Bar and in-room dining.
The restaurants and bars showcase New Zealand produce, local wines and craft beers.
The Living Room serves share-style menus designed for gatherings and occasions.
The Pantry is a waterfront spot for coffee, fresh pastries and comfort food.
The Spa at Park Hyatt Auckland offers a wide range of treatments.
The fitness centre has cardiovascular, strength and weight-training equipment.
Rooms and suites have floor-to-ceiling windows.
Rooms have Le Labo bath amenities.
The Harbour Suite can connect to another room to create a two-bedroom suite.
EV charging is available in the hotel's car park.

highlights.text: Interiors are by Conran and Partners London, punctuated by traditional Maori art.
Captain's Bar has a fireplace and an outdoor terrace with waterfront views, serving a selection of rums and classic cocktails with a local twist.
Onemata is a waterfront restaurant with seasonal menus built on local produce.
Some rooms have a private rooftop balcony with views of the Viaduct Harbour and the city skyline.
The infinity pool looks out over Wynyard Quarter's Lighter Basin, with a pool deck for sunshine.

considerations.text: Auckland Airport is 21 kilometres from the hotel.
A surcharge applies at the hotel's restaurants and bars on public holidays.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Park Hyatt Auckland
